title: 02 · USE by layer
description: Utilization, Saturation, Errors for each resource layer: software resource, runtime, container, host, Postgres, Kafka.

options.content: **Each layer has its own limit.** Utilization only means something against the limit of that same layer. Order of reading: Errors, Saturation, then Utilization.

panels.title: DB pool: in use, max, waiting
Admission: in handler and waiting
panels.description: Requests waiting here are not yet counted in api's duration.

panels.title: Inventory lock: wait p99
panels.description: Time a checkout waits for api's one inventory lock. Off-CPU time: the thread uses no CPU while it waits.

panels.title: Inventory lock: utilization
panels.description: Share of time the lock is held. By M/M/1 the mean wait is utilization / (1 - utilization) times the hold time.

panels.title: Event loop lag p99
panels.description: Saturation of a single-threaded event loop: work waiting for the loop to be free.

panels.title: Process CPU (cores)
panels.description: The event loop is one thread: work on it uses at most about 1 core, whatever the limit.

panels.title: CPU user against system (cores)
panels.description: From the container's cpu.stat. System time is the kernel working for the process: syscalls such as writes to a socket, a pipe or a file.

panels.title: PSI cpu per container (seconds waited per second)
panels.description: May be empty if the kernel has PSI off.

panels.title: OOM kills (10 minutes)
panels.description: When a container's main process is killed, the container restarts with a new cgroup and its own counter starts at 0. The host line still counts that kill.

panels.title: Load (1 min) vs CPU count
panels.description: Load above the CPU count for long: a run queue, which is CPU saturation.

panels.title: Host PSI: CPU and memory (seconds waited per second)
Time Postgres spends executing (seconds per second)
panels.description: By Little's Law, this is the mean number of queries running inside Postgres.

panels.title: Wait events (mean backends waiting)
panels.description: Sampled every 100 ms from pg_stat_activity. IO / WALSync: waiting for a WAL fsync (a commit or the WAL writer). IO / DataFileSync: mostly the checkpointer flushing table files.

panels.title: Mean WAL sync time
panels.description: Every commit waits for one of these. It grows when the disk under the WAL is busy.

panels.title: WAL written per second
panels.description: The first change to a page after a checkpoint writes an image of the whole page to WAL, so WAL jumps right after each checkpoint.

panels.title: Checkpoints in the last minute, by kind
panels.description: timed: checkpoint_timeout fired. requested: WAL reached max_wal_size (or someone ran CHECKPOINT).

panels.title: Checkpoint write and sync (seconds per second)
panels.description: Both counters move once per checkpoint, when it ends. Write time includes the pauses that spread a checkpoint out, so a long write is healthy. Sync time is the burst of flushes at the end.

panels.title: TCP segments retransmitted/s
panels.description: Counted by the kernel in each container's own network namespace. Near 0 on a healthy network.

panels.title: RTO timeouts and tail loss probes/s
panels.description: Each one is a sender that waited for a lost segment. On Linux an RTO waits at least 200 ms.

panels.title: Sockets in TIME_WAIT
panels.description: The side that closes first keeps the socket for 60 s. About closes per second x 60.

panels.title: IOPS by device
panels.description: Completed I/Os per second as the host sees each disk. A cgroup IOPS limit holds I/O back before it reaches this count.

panels.title: Await (mean time per I/O)
panels.description: Queue time in the device plus service time, like iostat's w_await and r_await.

panels.title: Busy share (utilization)
panels.description: Share of time with at least one I/O in flight, like iostat's %util. A disk that serves I/Os in parallel can take more work at 100%.

panels.title: Queue (mean I/Os in flight)
panels.description: Saturation, like iostat's aqu-sz. By Little's Law it is IOPS times await.

panels.title: api heap by pool against the old gen max
panels.description: Serial collector pools: Eden Space and Survivor Space are the young generation, Tenured Gen the old one. Old gen usage grows between full GCs.

panels.title: GC pause p99
panels.description: Every pause stops all application threads. A request in flight during a pause waits for it.

panels.title: api GC pauses (pauses per bucket)
panels.description: One cell per pause-length bucket and interval. A full GC shows as a cell far above the young GC band.

panels.title: GC runs per second by collector and cause
panels.description: Copy is the young collector, MarkSweepCompact the full one.

panels.title: Allocation rate
panels.description: Bytes allocated in the young generation per second, counted at each GC.

panels.title: Live data after full GC against the old gen max
panels.description: What a full GC could not free. Close to the max: each GC frees little, so the next one comes soon.

panels.title: Pinned virtual threads per second
panels.description: JFR jdk.VirtualThreadPinned events above 1 ms: a virtual thread blocked while it could not leave its carrier thread.

panels.title: Time pinned per second (carriers blocked)
panels.description: Seconds of pinned blocking per second, about the number of carriers blocked at once. api has 2 carriers, one per core.

panels.title: api: where the CPU goes
panels.description: Summed over the time range. Width is a share of CPU samples, and the x-axis is not time. Narrow the range to the incident, and compare with a range before it.
